summary: An X-guard companion separating the course’s routes underneath the opponent from sweeping finishes and counter responses.
description: Navigate The Marcelo X Guard by deciding whether your problem is entry, finishing a sweep or maintaining the position.
overview: The first two volumes emphasize entries, the third concentrates on finishes and the fourth collects responses and transitions. Collar and sleeve examples appear in the outline alongside butterfly and shin-to-shin routes.

guide.display_title: Marcelo Garcia: X-Guard Entries and Sweeps

fits: You want to distinguish a failed X-guard entry from a stalled stand-up sweep or an opponent’s pummel.
consider_alternative_if: For a gi single-leg-X emphasis with sleeve/lapel sweep variations, compare Adam Wardzinski’s guide.

includes: Butterfly, grip-based and shin-to-shin entry sections.
Stand-up, push-back and tilt finishes; pummel, backstep and single-leg-X transition material.
limits: Several entries and counters explicitly use collar or sleeve grips; this is not exclusively a no-gi syllabus.

start_here.title: Track the stage at which the exchange stalls
start_here.task: Use the chapter groupings to label an X-guard exchange as entry, finish or counter response. For a stand-up sweep problem, compare the initial finish with the following opponent-pulls-away lesson. For a connection lost before the finish, search the entry or pummel sections instead.
start_here.section: Volume 3: X-Guard Finishes - Stand up sweep — 0 (course timestamp)
